SECOND ARCHIVE PASS, 2026-08-24: Sprint 16 (BL-569..BL-578) and Sprint 17b (BL-596..BL-604) both closed on this date, and their nineteen completed items moved to archive/backlog-complete-2026-08-24.json. The hot file is EMPTY, which is the resting state this convention intends between sprints — the next sprint's items are authored fresh against the authority docs rather than inherited. (Sprint 17's own eleven items are RETAINED here by the merge of 2026-08-24: that sprint closed under the other reading of this note, with prose archived and metadata kept, and this merge does not re-archive another session's bookkeeping.)
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

items.title: A lens legend takes the minimap's space, for every lens
items.design: Ruled 2026-08-25 (Ben, looking at the live Throughput lens): "when a lens needs a legend, it takes the minimap space" — the flush-left-of-the-minimap anchor is retired, because it put the key over the always-open Selection band and read as sloppy. Design settled in docs/ui/LENSES.md § legend chromes; read it before implementing. Scope: move the gradient-bar chrome (begin_lens_key) into the minimap rect and let the minimap yield; the count-driven keys already sit in the right chrome column above the minimap and should be reconciled to the same rule rather than left as a second idiom. Two consequences fall out and are deliberately part of this item: the BL-376 foreground-list + opaque-fill workaround becomes unnecessary once the legend owns its rect (it was the right fix for the wrong layout), which also dissolves the standing defect that six of the seven gradient keys were unreadable under the band; and the item must answer what the minimap does while displaced — hidden outright, or restored the moment the lens clears. A live click is required, per the UI rule. CANCELLED 2026-08-25, by Ben on seeing the merged build: "Looks fantastic, probably better than my direct instruction to fill minimap space." Sprint 17b had already moved every legend into one chrome home — the minimap HEADER, growing upward into the column — which answers the complaint that prompted the ruling (a key popped out over the Selection band) without taking the minimap's own rect. The 2026-08-25 ruling is therefore superseded by its own author in favour of what shipped. The z-order half of this item is also moot: 17b's region overlaps no window, so the foreground-list workaround was dropped at the merge rather than generalised. RENUMBERED BL-604 -> BL-609 on 2026-08-25. Sprint 17b and Sprint 18 ran concurrently on 2026-08-24 and both drew BL-604 from the same fresh id range for different work; 17b's landed in a FROZEN cold archive and holds the majority of live citations, so Sprint 18's id moved instead. items.title: The partition runs before roads; every province's settlement exists when the lattice is laid
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ruled 2026-08-25 (Ben, resolving NR-640 as option c): reorder the homeworld pipeline to ... institutional history -> provinces (+ ensure_province_anchor_centres) -> roads -> corporations -> markets -> laws. The partition drops roads from its inputs (partition ruling 2's binding half OVERTURNED, recorded in PROVINCES.md), so the road-bind divisor retires from the cost model, the partition's recompute contract (P6) trivially excludes roads, and the anchor foundings exist BEFORE generate_roads - they take local streets and spurs like any village, ending the off-lattice class entirely. Corporations stay after roads so placement reach reads the real network. Harness consequences owned here: province_partition_harness drops its road-bind rows and keeps P6/P7 against the new input set; road_generation_harness strengthens R3 back to every-centre-on-lattice and retires R3b. Design settled in PROVINCES.md (rulings 2/3) and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md (the run order) - read before implementing. COMPLETION: Landed 2026-08-25 (Agent W3, ef20f9fe; merged main). Two-call partition shape (early homeworld + canonical end-of-gen rebuild, P6-guarded); road-bind divisor deleted; all 1,344 centres on the lattice (27 street-only survivors, counted); roaded tiles 1,511 -> 3,082; world_audit/partition/road/determinism all green.

items.title: Razing demotes a settlement to a razed tier; the province keeps its capture anchor and rebuilding is cheap
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ruled 2026-08-25 (Ben: 'keep razed settlement as a settlement tier, so it's cheap to rebuild there'). raze_centre stops erasing: it sets a persistent razed state - population zeroed, no labour/demand/agglomeration contribution, entity + name + tile + urban ground all kept, the centre still anchors its province (a ruin can be captured; the province-settlement invariant survives play). Rebuild: the ordinary growth pass re-settles a razed centre at a REDUCED gate (first-cut: half the promotion window; a data constant) back to scale 1, clearing the razed state. Serialisation: the razed field rides the centre record, save v14 -> v15, strict refusal. population_dynamics P3 rows re-specified from erasure to demotion; a new row proves razed -> regrown round-trip. ACTIONS.json raze_centre entry updated. Design settled in POPULATION.md section Growth, decline and razing - read before implementing. COMPLETION: Landed 2026-08-25 (Agent W3, d8f7ed3a; merged main). razed bool beside province_anchor; raze demotes to a scale-1 ruin that still anchors; excluded from labour/demand/habitability/migration; re-settles at half the promotion window; save v14->v15; population_dynamics 31 assertions incl. the razed->regrown round-trip.

items.title: A glyph per settlement tier: the canvas reads as a world of many population centres
items.author: Ben
items.design: Raised by Ben 2026-08-25, straight after the flood-field warm-start fix: now that the world genuinely carries a settlement per province (BL-623, provinces before roads) plus the razed tier (BL-624), the canvas should SHOW that density - today the population-centre mark does not distinguish scale, so a metropolis and a village read identically and the world looks emptier than it is. Work: one glyph per tier of population_centre_component.scale (1-5, village -> metropolis), plus a distinct mark for a razed centre (BL-624's orthogonal bool - a ruin should read as a ruin, not vanish). Glyphs live in src/ui/icons.{hpp,cpp} under the (dl, centre, r, colour) contract and are catalogued in docs/ui/ICONS.md in the same change; identity colours stay in presentation.hpp. Zoom behaviour follows the existing detail_level rules so low zoom does not smear five glyph shapes into noise. ACTIONS.json untouched unless a control changes; question_log entry owed if the surface's question materially changes. MEASURED 2026-08-25 (Ben reported no settlements visible in play; count_clusters diagnostic over the canonical world): the homeworld carries 1,823 population centres, and body_surface_canvas's conurbation clustering (Chebyshev <= 3, TRANSITIVE chaining - authored for 20-40 centres/body) collapses them to 49 drawn marks; scales run 1,757/52/11/3/0 for 1-5, so the surviving marks are mostly the smallest skyline. The item's scope is therefore the DISPLAY MODEL, not only glyph shapes: the clustering rule must be revisited for the post-BL-623 density (options: per-tier clustering, a smaller radius, or a zoom-laddered LOD where far zoom shows scale>=3 plus a density read and close zoom shows every centre). A skyline glyph already exists (icons::settlement, towers rise with tier); distinct-per-tier shapes and the razed mark build on it. BUILT 2026-08-25 with the LOD ladder (Ben's pick): far zoom (draw_r <= 7, the coarse-fill pivot) draws scale>=3 skylines and renders every smaller centre as a dim civic density dot; mid zoom (7-14) adds towns; close zoom (>=14, the texture pivot) draws every centre including villages, and razed centres surface as the new outline-only ruin glyph (icons::settlement_razed). Clustering removed; gather is sorted by centre id for deterministic overdraw; vertical cull added (1,800+ centres are real vertices). Verified via pop_markers + settlement_labels captures: the zoom framing that previously drew one mark now shows the settled region.
